originalTitle: NSE indices rejig: Vodafone Idea, Wipro part of major changes in Nifty Next 50 and Nifty 100. Check full list
simplifiedContent: The National Stock Exchange (NSE) is making some big changes to its lists of important companies, called indices. This change will happen on September 30 and will affect three main lists: Nifty 500, Nifty 100, and Nifty Next 50. Some companies, like Vodafone Idea and Wipro, will be added to these lists, while others will be removed. This matters because being on one of these lists can affect how many people invest in a company and how well it does. The full list of changes will show which companies are being added or removed from these important lists.

originalTitle: Nifty rejig: IT major Wipro to move out of benchmark index after BSE gets inclusion
simplifiedContent: Here's a simplified explanation of the news: Wipro, a big IT company, will no longer be part of India's main stock market index, called the Nifty index. Instead, BSE Ltd will join the index. This change will happen on September 30, 2026. BSE was added to the index because its market value met a certain requirement, specifically its average market value over the past six months was high enough. This matters because being part of the Nifty index can affect how investors view and trade a company's stock.

originalTitle: Intel shares drop 5% after announcing $15 billion offering to support AI growth
simplifiedContent: Intel, a big company that makes computer chips, announced that it's going to sell more of its shares to raise $15 billion. The company wants to use this money to grow its business, especially in the area of artificial intelligence (AI). As a result, the value of Intel's existing shares dropped by over 5%. This matters because it shows that the company is trying to invest in its future, but it also means that people who already own Intel shares might see their investment decrease in value. The money raised will help Intel strengthen its financial position and meet the increasing demand for AI-related products.

originalTitle: Nippon India Equity buys stake in Iris Clothings that has risen 250% in five years
simplifiedContent: Nippon India Equity has invested in a company called Iris Clothings. The company's stock price has gone up by 250% over the past five years, which means it has more than tripled in value. This is a significant increase, and the stock has been performing well for over a year, continuously reaching new highs. As a result, investing in Iris Clothings has created a lot of wealth for its shareholders. This matters because it shows that Iris Clothings is a strong performer in the stock market, making it an attractive investment opportunity.

originalTitle: Wall Street slips ahead of inflation data, crude oil surges
simplifiedContent: The stock market, also known as Wall Street, is experiencing a small decline. This means that the value of most stocks is going down slightly. The main stock market indexes, such as the S&P 500, Dow Jones, and Nasdaq, are showing small changes, with the S&P 500 barely rising and the others falling. This is happening as people wait for important information about inflation, which is a measure of how much prices are rising. The small decline in the market may be a sign that investors are being cautious ahead of this important data.

originalTitle: Vodafone Idea Q1 Results: Net loss narrows to  ₹3,754 crore, ARPU rises to  ₹195; key highlights
simplifiedContent: Vodafone Idea, a company that provides phone and internet services, recently shared its financial results for the April to June period. The company still lost money, but the loss was smaller than last year, coming in at ₹3,754 crore. This is an improvement from the ₹6,608 crore loss they had last year. The company's total revenue, or the amount of money they made from their services, also increased slightly to ₹11,689 crore. This matters because it shows that the company is making progress and possibly becoming more stable, which could be important for people who invest in the company.
